sanskrit: caran sa vividhān mārgān ratheṣu rathayūthapaḥ trigartānāṃ suśarmāṇam ārcchad rukmarathaṃ raṇe
english: Ranging across many paths as a chieftain among chariot-warriors, he encountered Suśarman of the Trigartasthe one with the golden chariot—in battle.

sanskrit: tau vyāvaharatāṃ tatra mahātmānau mahābalau anyonyam abhigarjantau goṣṭhe govṛṣabhāv iva
english: Those two great-souled and mighty warriors fought there, roaring at each other like two bulls in a cattle-pen.

sanskrit: tato rathābhyāṃ rathinau vyatiyāya samantataḥ śarān vyasṛjatāṃ śīghraṃ toyadhārā ghanāv iva
english: Then those two chariot-warriors, circling each other on their chariots from all sides, swiftly released arrows like rain-laden clouds pouring streams of water.

sanskrit: anyonyaṃ cātisaṃrabdhau viceratur amarṣaṇau kṛtāstrau niśitair bāṇair asiśaktigadābhṛtau
english: Extremely enraged at each other, impatient and skilled in weapons, bearing sword, spear, and mace, they ranged about, piercing each other with sharp arrows.

sanskrit: tato rājā suśarmāṇaṃ vivyādha daśabhiḥ śaraiḥ pañcabhiḥ pañcabhiś cāsya vivyādha caturo hayān
english: Then the king pierced Suśarman with ten arrows, and with five and five more he pierced his four horses.

sanskrit: tathaiva matsyarājānaṃ suśarmā yuddhadurmadaḥ pañcāśatā śitair bāṇair vivyādha paramāstravit
english: Likewise Suśarman, frenzied in battle and a supreme master of weapons, pierced the king of Matsya with fifty sharp arrows.

sanskrit: tataḥ sainyaṃ samāvṛtya matsyarājasuśarmaṇoḥ nābhyajānaṃs tadānyonyaṃ pradoṣe rajasāvṛte
english: Then the armies of both the Matsya king and Suśarman, enveloped in the dust of dusk, could no longer distinguish one another.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tamasābhiplute loke rajasā caiva bhārata vyatiṣṭhan vai muhūrtaṃ tu vyūḍhānīkāḥ prahāriṇaḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: O Bhārata, with the world flooded by darkness and dust, the arrayed armies of combatants halted for a moment.

sanskrit: tato 'ndhakāraṃ praṇudann udatiṣṭhata candramāḥ kurvāṇo vimalāṃ rātriṃ nandayan kṣatriyān yudhi
english: Then the moon rose, dispelling the darkness, making the night bright and bringing joy to the Kṣatriyas in battle.

sanskrit: tataḥ prakāśam āsādya punar yuddham avartata ghorarūpaṃ tatas te sma nāvekṣanta parasparam
english: Then, as light returned, the terrible battle resumed; even so, they could no longer properly observe one another.

sanskrit: tataḥ suśarmā traigartaḥ saha bhrātrā yavīyasā abhyadravan matsyarājaṃ rathavrātena sarvaśaḥ
english: Then Suśarman of Trigarta, together with his younger brother, charged at the king of Matsya from all sides with a multitude of chariots.

sanskrit: tato rathābhyāṃ praskandya bhrātarau kṣatriyarṣabhau gadāpāṇī susaṃrabdhau samabhyadravatāṃ hayān
english: Then those two brothers, bulls among Kṣatriyas, leaped down from their chariots and, maces in hand, full of fury, charged toward the horses.

sanskrit: tathaiva teṣāṃ tu balāni tāni; kruddhāny athānyonyam abhidravanti gadāsikhaḍgaiś ca paraśvadhaiś ca; prāsaiś ca tīkṣṇāgrasupītadhāraiḥ
english: Likewise their forces, enraged, charged at one another with maces, swords, axes, and lances with sharp points and well-whetted edges.

sanskrit: balaṃ tu matsyasya balena rājā; sarvaṃ trigartādhipatiḥ suśarmā pramathya jitvā ca prasahya matsyaṃ; virāṭam ojasvinam abhyadhāvat
english: But Suśarman, the lord of Trigarta, having crushed and forcibly overcome all the forces of Matsya with his own forces, charged at the mighty Virāṭa of Matsya.

sanskrit: tau nihatya pṛthag dhuryāv ubhau ca pārṣṇisārathī virathaṃ matsyarājānaṃ jīvagrāham agṛhṇatām
english: Having slain separately the draft-horses and both rear-guard charioteers, those two seized the king of Matsya alive, his chariot rendered useless.

sanskrit: tam unmathya suśarmā tu rudatīṃ vadhukām iva syandanaṃ svaṃ samāropya prayayau śīghravāhanaḥ
english: Suśarman, having seized him and placed him on his own chariot like a weeping bride, sped away with swift horses.

sanskrit: tasmin gṛhīte virathe virāṭe balavattare prādravanta bhayān matsyās trigartair arditā bhṛśam
english: When the mighty Virāṭa was thus captured and left without a chariot, the Matsyas fled in fear, greatly tormented by the Trigartasas.

sanskrit: teṣu saṃtrāsyamāneṣu kuntīputro yudhiṣṭhiraḥ abhyabhāṣan mahābāhuṃ bhīmasenam ariṃdamam
english: While they were being routed in terror, Yudhiṣṭhira, son of Kuntī, addressed the mighty-armed Bhīmasena, the subduer of foes.

sanskrit: matsyarājaḥ parāmṛṣṭas trigartena suśarmaṇā taṃ mokṣaya mahābāho na gacched dviṣatāṃ vaśam
english: The king of Matsya has been seized by Suśarman of Trigarta—free him, O mighty-armed one; let him not fall under the power of our enemies.

sanskrit: uṣitāḥ smaḥ sukhaṃ sarve sarvakāmaiḥ supūjitāḥ bhīmasena tvayā kāryā tasya vāsasya niṣkṛtiḥ
english: We have all dwelt in comfort, honored with every wish fulfilled; O Bhīmasena, you must repay that hospitality now.

sanskrit: bhīmasena uvāca aham enaṃ paritrāsye śāsanāt tava pārthiva paśya me sumahat karma yudhyataḥ saha śatrubhiḥ
english: Bhīmasena said: By your command, O king, I shall rescue him. Behold my great deed as I fight against the enemies.

sanskrit: svabāhubalam āśritya tiṣṭha tvaṃ bhrātṛbhiḥ saha ekāntam āśrito rājan paśya me 'dya parākramam
english: Relying on the strength of my own arms, stand aside with your brothers, O king; withdrawing to one side, witness my prowess today.

sanskrit: suskandho 'yaṃ mahāvṛkṣo gadārūpa iva sthitaḥ enam eva samārujya drāvayiṣyāmi śātravān
english: This great tree with its sturdy trunk stands like a mace; uprooting it, I shall rout the enemies.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca taṃ mattam iva mātaṅgaṃ vīkṣamāṇaṃ vanaspatim abravīd bhrātaraṃ vīraṃ dharmarājo yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: As that one, like a maddened elephant, was eyeing the forest lord, Dharmarāja Yudhiṣṭhira spoke to his heroic brother.

sanskrit: mā bhīma sāhasaṃ kārṣīs tiṣṭhatv eṣa vanaspatiḥ mā tvā vṛkṣeṇa karmāṇi kurvāṇam atimānuṣam janāḥ samavabudhyeran bhīmo 'yam iti bhārata
english: Do not act rashly, O Bhīma; let this forest tree remain. O Bhārata, lest people, seeing you perform superhuman deeds with a tree, recognize you as Bhīma.

sanskrit: anyad evāyudhaṃ kiṃ cit pratipadyasva mānuṣam cāpaṃ vā yadi vā śaktiṃ nistriṃśaṃ vā paraśvadham
english: Take up some other, more human weapon instead—a bow, a lance, a sword, or an axe.

sanskrit: yad eva mānuṣaṃ bhīma bhaved anyair alakṣitam tad evāyudham ādāya mokṣayāśu mahīpatim
english: Whatever human weapon, O Bhīma, would go unnoticed by others—take up that weapon and quickly free the lord of the earth.

sanskrit: yamau ca cakrarakṣau te bhavitārau mahābalau vyūhataḥ samare tāta matsyarājaṃ parīpsataḥ
english: And the two mighty twins shall be your wheel-guards; they will array themselves in battle, dear one, seeking to protect the king of Matsya.

sanskrit: tataḥ samastās te sarve turagān abhyacodayan divyam astraṃ vikurvāṇās trigartān pratyamarṣaṇāḥ
english: Then all of them together urged their horses forward, invoking divine weapons and full of fury toward the Trigartasas.

sanskrit: tān nivṛttarathān dṛṣṭvā pāṇḍavān sā mahācamūḥ vairāṭī paramakruddhā yuyudhe paramādbhutam
english: Seeing the Pāṇḍavas with their chariots turned back toward them, that great army of Virāṭa, supremely enraged, fought in a most wondrous manner.

sanskrit: sahasraṃ nyavadhīt tatra kuntīputro yudhiṣṭhiraḥ bhīmaḥ saptaśatān yodhān paralokam adarśayat nakulaś cāpi saptaiva śatāni prāhiṇoc charaiḥ
english: There Yudhiṣṭhira, son of Kuntī, slew a thousand; Bhīma dispatched seven hundred warriors to the next world; Nakula too sent seven hundred with his arrows.

sanskrit: śatāni trīṇi śūrāṇāṃ sahadevaḥ pratāpavān yudhiṣṭhirasamādiṣṭo nijaghne puruṣarṣabhaḥ bhittvā tāṃ mahatīṃ senāṃ trigartānāṃ nararṣabha
english: The glorious Sahadeva, that bull among men, commanded by Yudhiṣṭhira, slew three hundred heroes, breaking through that great army of the Trigartasas, O bull among men.

sanskrit: tato yudhiṣṭhiro rājā tvaramāṇo mahārathaḥ abhidrutya suśarmāṇaṃ śarair abhyatudad bhṛśam
english: Then king Yudhiṣṭhira, that great chariot-warrior, swiftly charging at Suśarman, struck him hard with arrows.

sanskrit: suśarmāpi susaṃkruddhas tvaramāṇo yudhiṣṭhiram avidhyan navabhir bāṇaiś caturbhiś caturo hayān
english: Suśarman too, greatly enraged, swiftly pierced Yudhiṣṭhira with nine arrows and his four horses with four each.

sanskrit: tato rājann āśukārī kuntīputro vṛkodaraḥ samāsādya suśarmāṇam aśvān asya vyapothayat
english: Then, O king, Vṛkodara, son of Kuntī, swift in action, charging at Suśarman, slaughtered his horses.

sanskrit: pṛṣṭhagopau ca tasyātha hatvā paramasāyakaiḥ athāsya sārathiṃ kruddho rathopasthād apāharat
english: And having slain his two rear-guards with supreme arrows, enraged, he then dragged his charioteer down from the chariot-platform.

sanskrit: cakrarakṣaś ca śūraś ca śoṇāśvo nāma viśrutaḥ sa bhayād dvairathaṃ dṛṣṭvā traigartaṃ prājahat tadā
english: And the wheel-guard, the renowned hero called Śoṇāśva, seeing the Trigarta in single-chariot combat, then fled in fear.

sanskrit: tato virāṭaḥ praskandya rathād atha suśarmaṇaḥ gadām asya parāmṛśya tam evājaghnivān balī sa cacāra gadāpāṇir vṛddho 'pi taruṇo yathā
english: Then Virāṭa, having leaped down from Suśarman's chariot, grabbed his mace and struck him with it; that powerful man moved about mace in hand like a young man, though aged.

sanskrit: bhīmas tu bhīmasaṃkāśo rathāt praskandya kuṇḍalī trigartarājam ādatta siṃhaḥ kṣudramṛgaṃ yathā
english: But Bhīma, dreadful in appearance and earring-adorned, leaped from his chariot and seized the king of Trigarta as a lion seizes a small animal.

sanskrit: tasmin gṛhīte virathe trigartānāṃ mahārathe abhajyata balaṃ sarvaṃ traigartaṃ tadbhayāturam
english: When that great chariot-warrior of the Trigartasas was seized and left without his chariot, the entire Trigarta army broke and fled, stricken with terror.

sanskrit: nivartya gās tataḥ sarvāḥ pāṇḍuputrā mahābalāḥ avajitya suśarmāṇaṃ dhanaṃ cādāya sarvaśaḥ
english: Then the mighty sons of Pāṇḍu, having recovered all the cattle, having subdued Suśarman, and having seized all his wealth,

sanskrit: svabāhubalasamṃpannā hrīniṣedhā yatavratāḥ saṃgrāmaśiraso madhye tāṃ rātriṃ sukhino 'vasan
english: endowed with the strength of their own arms, restrained by modesty, steadfast in their vows, passed that night happily in the midst of the battlefield.

sanskrit: tato virāṭaḥ kaunteyān atimānuṣavikramān arcayām āsa vittena mānena ca mahārathān
english: Then Virāṭa honored those great chariot-warriors, the sons of Kuntī, of superhuman valor, with wealth and esteem.

sanskrit: virāṭa uvāca yathaiva mama ratnāni yuṣmākaṃ tāni vai tathā kāryaṃ kuruta taiḥ sarve yathākāmaṃ yathāsukham
english: Virāṭa said: Whatever jewels are mine are equally yours; use them all as you desire and as pleases you.

sanskrit: dadāny alaṃkṛtāḥ kanyā vasūni vividhāni ca manasaś cāpy abhipretaṃ yad vaḥ śatrunibarhaṇāḥ
english: I shall give you adorned maidens and various riches, and whatever else your hearts desire, O destroyers of foes.

sanskrit: yuṣmākaṃ vikramād adya mukto 'haṃ svastimān iha tasmād bhavanto matsyānām īśvarāḥ sarva eva hi
english: By your valor I am today freed and stand here in safety; therefore, all of you are indeed lords over the Matsyas.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tathābhivādinaṃ matsyaṃ kauraveyāḥ pṛthak pṛthak ūcuḥ prāñjalayaḥ sarve yudhiṣṭhirapurogamāḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: All the descendants of the Kurus, led by Yudhiṣṭhira, with joined palms, each replied to Matsya who had spoken thus.

sanskrit: pratinandāma te vākyaṃ sarvaṃ caiva viśāṃ pate etenaiva pratītāḥ smo yat tvaṃ mukto 'dya śatrubhiḥ
english: We receive your words with joy, O lord of the people, and we are satisfied by this alone—that you are today freed from your enemies.

sanskrit: athābravīt prītamanā matsyarājo yudhiṣṭhiram punar eva mahābāhur virāṭo rājasattamaḥ ehi tvām abhiṣekṣyāmi matsyarājo 'stu no bhavān
english: Then with a joyful heart, the king of Matsya, the mighty-armed Virāṭa, best of kings, once again said to Yudhiṣṭhira: Come, I shall consecrate you—be our king of Matsya.

sanskrit: manasaś cāpy abhipretaṃ yat te śatrunibarhaṇa tat te 'haṃ saṃpradāsyāmi sarvam arhati no bhavān
english: And whatever your heart desires, O destroyer of foes, all of that I shall give you; you are worthy of our everything.

sanskrit: ratnāni gāḥ suvarṇaṃ ca maṇimuktam athāpi vā vaiyāghrapadya viprendra sarvathaiva namo 'stu te
english: Jewels, cattle, gold, gems and pearls—O descendant of Vyāghrapāda, O lord of brāhmaṇas, to you all homage in every way.

sanskrit: tvatkṛte hy adya paśyāmi rājyam ātmānam eva ca yataś ca jātaḥ saṃrambhaḥ sa ca śatrur vaśaṃ gataḥ
english: For because of you I today see both my kingdom and myself; and the one from whom the conflict arose—that enemy too has been brought under control.

sanskrit: tato yudhiṣṭhiro matsyaṃ punar evābhyabhāṣata pratinandāmi te vākyaṃ manojñaṃ matsya bhāṣase
english: Then Yudhiṣṭhira once again addressed Matsya: I joyfully accept your words; you speak pleasingly, O Matsya.

sanskrit: ānṛśaṃsyaparo nityaṃ susukhaḥ satataṃ bhava gacchantu dūtās tvaritaṃ nagaraṃ tava pārthiva suhṛdāṃ priyam ākhyātuṃ ghoṣayantu ca te jayam
english: Be ever dedicated to non-cruelty and always be very happy. Let swift messengers go to your city, O king, to announce the glad tidings to your friends and proclaim your victory.

sanskrit: tatas tadvacanān matsyo dūtān rājā samādiśat ācakṣadhvaṃ puraṃ gatvā saṃgrāme vijayaṃ mama
english: Then, at those words, king Matsya instructed the messengers: Go to the city and announce my victory in battle.

sanskrit: kumārāḥ samalaṃkṛtya paryāgacchantu me purāt vāditrāṇi ca sarvāṇi gaṇikāś ca svalaṃkṛtāḥ
english: Let the princes come adorned from my city, and all the musical instruments, and the courtesans well-adorned.

sanskrit: te gatvā kevalāṃ rātrim atha sūryodayaṃ prati virāṭasya purābhyāśe dūtā jayam aghoṣayan
english: Those messengers, having traveled through the entire night and toward sunrise, proclaimed the victory near the city of Virāṭa.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca yāte trigartaṃ matsye tu paśūṃs tān svān parīpsati duryodhanaḥ sahāmātyo virāṭam upayād atha
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: While the Matsya king had gone toward the Trigartasas to recover his cattle, Duryodhana with his ministers then marched against Virāṭa.

sanskrit: bhīṣmo droṇaś ca karṇaś ca kṛpaś ca paramāstravit drauṇiś ca saubalaś caiva tathā duḥśāsanaḥ prabhuḥ
english: Bhīṣma, Droṇa, Karṇa, and Kṛpa the supreme weapon-master, Drauṇi and the son of Subala, and the lord Duḥśāsana—

sanskrit: viviṃśatir vikarṇaś ca citrasenaś ca vīryavān durmukho duḥsahaś caiva ye caivānye mahārathāḥ
english: Viviṃśati, Vikarṇa, the valiant Citrasena, Durmukha, Duḥsaha—and whatever other great chariot-warriors there were.

sanskrit: ete matsyān upāgamya virāṭasya mahīpateḥ ghoṣān vidrāvya tarasā godhanaṃ jahrur ojasā
english: These, having come against the Matsyas, the subjects of king Virāṭa, swiftly scattered the settlements and with force carried off the cattle.

sanskrit: ṣaṣṭiṃ gavāṃ sahasrāṇi kuravaḥ kālayanti te mahatā rathavaṃśena parivārya samantataḥ
english: The Kurus were driving sixty thousand cows, surrounding them on all sides with a great multitude of chariots.

sanskrit: gopālānāṃ tu ghoṣeṣu hanyatāṃ tair mahārathaiḥ ārāvaḥ sumahān āsīt saṃprahāre bhayaṃkare
english: In the settlements of the cowherds, as they were being slaughtered by those great chariot-warriors, a tremendous uproar arose in the terrifying encounter.

sanskrit: gavādhyakṣas tu saṃtrasto ratham āsthāya satvaraḥ jagāma nagarāyaiva parikrośaṃs tadārtavat
english: The superintendent of cattle, terrified, quickly mounted a chariot and went directly to the city, crying out piteously in distress.

sanskrit: sa praviśya puraṃ rājño nṛpaveśmābhyayāt tataḥ avatīrya rathāt tūrṇam ākhyātuṃ praviveśa ha
english: Having entered the city, he went then to the king's palace; quickly alighting from the chariot, he entered to deliver the news.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā bhūmiṃjayaṃ nāma putraṃ matsyasya māninam tasmai tat sarvam ācaṣṭa rāṣṭrasya paśukarṣaṇam
english: Seeing Bhūmiṃjaya, the proud son of Matsya, he reported to him all the plundering of the kingdom's cattle.

sanskrit: ṣaṣṭiṃ gavāṃ sahasrāṇi kuravaḥ kālayanti te tad vijetuṃ samuttiṣṭha godhanaṃ rāṣṭravardhanam
english: The Kurus are driving away sixty thousand cows—arise to conquer that wealth of cattle, the prosperity of the kingdom.

sanskrit: rājaputra hitaprepsuḥ kṣipraṃ niryāhi vai svayam tvāṃ hi matsyo mahīpālaḥ śūnyapālam ihākarot
english: O prince, wishing your welfare, please go out yourself quickly; the Matsya king, lord of the earth, has appointed you here as guardian in his absence.

sanskrit: tvayā pariṣado madhye ślāghate sa narādhipaḥ putro mamānurūpaś ca śūraś ceti kulodvahaḥ
english: That lord of men praises you in the assembly, saying: 'My son is suited to me, a hero, and the upholder of our lineage.'

sanskrit: iṣvastre nipuṇo yodhaḥ sadā vīraś ca me sutaḥ tasya tat satyam evāstu manuṣyendrasya bhāṣitam
english: 'A fighter skilled in archery and ever heroic is my son'—let the words of that lord of men prove true.

sanskrit: āvartaya kurūñ jitvā paśūn paśumatāṃ vara nirdahaiṣām anīkāni bhīmena śaratejasā
english: Turn back the Kurus after defeating them and recover the cattle, O best among the wealthy; burn their armies with the fierce blazing of your arrows.

sanskrit: dhanuścyutai rukmapuṅkhaiḥ śaraiḥ saṃnataparvabhiḥ dviṣatāṃ bhindhy anīkāni gajānām iva yūthapaḥ
english: With gold-feathered, well-jointed arrows loosed from the bow, pierce the enemies' armies like a bull-elephant leading a herd.

sanskrit: pāśopadhānāṃ jyātantrīṃ cāpadaṇḍāṃ mahāsvanām śaravarṇāṃ dhanurvīṇāṃ śatrumadhye pravādaya
english: Play the bow-vīṇā, whose strings are the bowstring, whose pillow is the arrow-notch, whose shaft is the handle, which resounds greatly and is adorned with arrows, in the midst of the enemies.

sanskrit: śvetā rajatasaṃkāśā rathe yujyantu te hayāḥ dhvajaṃ ca siṃhaṃ sauvarṇam ucchrayantu tavābhibhoḥ
english: Let white horses, resplendent as silver, be yoked to your chariot, and let the golden lion-banner be raised on high for you, O lord.

sanskrit: rukmapuṅkhāḥ prasannāgrā muktā hastavatā tvayā chādayantu śarāḥ sūryaṃ rājñām āyur nirodhinaḥ
english: Let your gold-feathered arrows with bright tips, released by your skillful hand—arrows that cut short the lives of kings—cover even the sun.

sanskrit: raṇe jitvā kurūn sarvān vajrapāṇir ivāsurān yaśo mahad avāpya tvaṃ praviśedaṃ puraṃ punaḥ
english: Having conquered all the Kurus in battle as Vajrapāṇi conquered the demons, having won great glory, enter this city again.

sanskrit: tvaṃ hi rāṣṭrasya paramā gatir matsyapateḥ sutaḥ gatimanto bhavantv adya sarve viṣayavāsinaḥ
english: You are the supreme refuge of the kingdom, son of the Matsya lord; let all the subjects of the realm today find their recourse through you.

sanskrit: strīmadhya uktas tenāsau tad vākyam abhayaṃkaram antaḥpure ślāghamāna idaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: Thus addressed in the midst of women, that one, boasting in the inner chambers, spoke this fearless-seeming word in response.

sanskrit: uttara uvāca adyāham anugaccheyaṃ dṛḍhadhanvā gavāṃ padam yadi me sārathiḥ kaś cid bhaved aśveṣu kovidaḥ
english: Uttara said: Today I would follow the tracks of the cattle, firm-bowed as I am, if only I had a charioteer who is skilled with horses.

sanskrit: tam eva nādhigacchāmi yo me yantā bhaven naraḥ paśyadhvaṃ sārathiṃ kṣipraṃ mama yuktaṃ prayāsyataḥ
english: But I cannot find the man who would be my driver; look quickly for a charioteer suitable for me as I am about to set out.
